issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the dismissal of a review application is not barred by res judicata merely because a petition challenging the original judgment was later withdrawn, when the review application was filed first.
material_facts: The review application against the High Court’s original judgment was filed before the petition seeking special leave to challenge that judgment.
The special leave petition challenging the original judgment was later withdrawn.
The present appeal challenged the High Court’s subsequent dismissal of the review application.
issues.conclusion: The objection that the appeal was barred by res judicata or analogous principles was rejected, and the appeal was held maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Applying K. Rajamouli v. A.V.K.N. Swamy, the Court held that dismissal of a special leave petition against the original judgment does not constitute res judicata against a special leave petition challenging the review order if the review application was filed before the petition against the original judgment. A different result may follow where review is sought after the special leave petition has been dismissed and after long delay.

predicates.appeal_challenges_review_dismissal: The party brought an appeal challenging the dismissal of its review application.
predicates.review_filed_before_challenge_to_origina: The party filed its review application before filing its petition challenging the original judgment.
predicates.original_judgment_challenge_withdrawn: The party withdrew its petition challenging the original judgment.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges dismissal of a review application filed before the challenge to the original judgment, withdrawal of that challenge does not bar the appeal by res judicata.

issues.legal_issue: A review application should not be dismissed where material evidence bearing on the decision was overlooked and the judgment contains apparent errors contradicted by the record.
material_facts: The review application challenged an appellate judgment concerning compensation for acquired tea-estate land and tea bushes.
The record included the government’s earlier proposed rate for the land, awards or estimates concerning similar nearby land, and government valuations for different categories of land.
The land was classified in the record as tea-class land, while the appellate judgment stated that there was no material showing it fell within the category of rural land with tea cultivation.
The appellate court did not itself fix compensation for the tea bushes after disagreeing with the lower court’s valuation.
The Supreme Court concluded that this material had escaped the appellate court’s notice, but did not decide what compensation should ultimately be awarded.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the judgment dismissing the review application was set aside, and the application was remitted to the High Court for hearing and disposal; the compensation relief was left for that court to determine.
issues.legal_principle: Order 47, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits review for an error apparent on the face of the record, but review is not a rehearing of an allegedly erroneous decision or an appeal in disguise; an error requiring a process of reasoning is not ordinarily apparent (Parsion Devi v. Sumitri Devi). The Court also relied on S. Nagaraj v. State of Karnataka for the duty to rectify or recall orders based on mistaken assumptions of fact where their implementation could have serious consequences. On the record in this case, overlooked evidence and a finding directly contrary to the land-classification material justified a further look at the judgment.

predicates.review_application_challenges_appellate_: A party sought review of an appellate judgment concerning compensation for acquired property.
predicates.record_contains_material_evidence_on_val: The record contains government valuations or comparable awards relevant to the value of the acquired property.
predicates.appellate_judgment_overlooks_material_ev: The appellate judgment does not address material valuation evidence in the record.
predicates.appellate_finding_conflicts_with_record: A finding in the appellate judgment conflicts with the property classification or other material evidence in the record.

issues.definition: When a review of an appellate compensation judgment concerns material valuation evidence that the judgment overlooked and a finding that conflicts with the record, the dismissal of review is set aside and the review is remitted.
